messages.author: 21e2646f0cc9f243
messages.subject: Changing hyper-parameter values
parts:
Hello, when run the inla() call, I get different values for my hyper parameters but the values for the fixed effects remains the same. Here is my code

``
# Creating the stacks
stk.e1 <- inla.stack(
  tag = 'point',
  data = list(y = df.full$n, numtrials = df.full$N),
  A = list(A, 1, 1),
  effects = list(
    s = indexs,
    rr = 1:length(df.full$`literate.women.sq`),
    data.frame(
      b0 = 1,
      x1 = df.full$`literate.women.sq`,
      x2 = df.full$`pob_hfa.sq`,
      x3 = df.full$`literate.women.sq:pob_hfa.sq`,
      x4 = df.full$`literate.men.sq:literate.women.sq`,
      x5 = df.full$`anc`,
      x6 = df.full$`literate.women.sq:lst.nights.sq`,
      x7 = df.full$`dpt3.sq`,
      x8 = df.full$`literate.men.sq:prec.log`,
      x9 = df.full$`literate.women.sq:pets.sq`
    )
  )
)

stk.p1 <- inla.stack(
  tag = "pred",
  data = list(y = NA, numtrials = NA),
  A = list(Ap,1,1),
  effects = list(
    s = indexs,
    rr = (length(pred.df$literate.women.sq) + 1):(length(pred.df$literate.women.sq) + nrow(pred.df)),
    data.frame(
      b0 = 1,
      x1 = pred.df$`literate.women.sq`,
      x2 = pred.df$`pob_hfa.sq`,
      x3 = pred.df$`literate.women.sq:pob_hfa.sq`,
      x4 = pred.df$`literate.men.sq:literate.women.sq`,
      x5 = pred.df$`anc`,
      x6 = pred.df$`literate.women.sq:lst.nights.sq`,
      x7 = pred.df$`dpt3.sq`,
      x8 = pred.df$`literate.men.sq:prec.log`,
      x9 = pred.df$`literate.women.sq:pets.sq`
     
    )
  )
)

# Specifying the priors and the formula --------------------------------------------------

hyper.prec = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(2, .5)))
formula <-
  y ~ 0 +
  b0 +
  x1 +
  x2 +
  x3 +
  x4 +
  x5 +
  x6 +
  x7 +
  x8 +
  x9 +
  f(s, model = spde) +
  f(rr, model = "iid", hyper = hyper.prec)

# The model ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# stk.full has stk.e and stk.p
stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e1)
set.seed(123)

#' The inla() call
mod <- inla(
  formula,
  family = "binomial",
  Ntrials = numtrials,
  data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),
  control.family = control.family(link = 'logit'),
  control.predictor = list(
    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1,
    A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)
  ),
  control.compute = list(config = TRUE, return.marginals.predictor = TRUE),
  num.threads = 7,
  verbose = F
)
summary(mod)

### First run
Model hyperparameters:
                    mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for s      177.177 211.997     23.266  114.471    724.156 55.473
Stdev for s        0.142   0.099      0.026    0.118      0.396  0.072
Precision for rr   1.541   0.372      0.953    1.493      2.409  1.395

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -985.87
 is computed
Posterior summaries for the linear predictor and the fitted values are computed
(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

### second run
Model hyperparameters:
                    mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for s      168.602 190.736     23.673   112.21    665.478 56.375
Stdev for s        0.144   0.097      0.029     0.12      0.393  0.077
Precision for rr   1.538   0.365      0.959     1.49      2.388  1.397

### Third run
Model hyperparameters:
                    mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for s      160.208 170.576     23.916  109.940    608.433 57.159
Stdev for s        0.146   0.099      0.029    0.121      0.402  0.077
Precision for rr   1.539   0.365      0.959    1.492      2.390  1.397

```

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Changing hyper-parameter values
parts:
This happens because because of that the hyperparameter optimisation optimise a
function that also require optimisation, and its running in parallel.

you can make it better using R-4.4 and the recent testing version, and also
reduce tolerance

control.inla = list(tolerance = ...)


which is default 0.005
